To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relative performance of various scheduling algorithms is independent of the variance in run-time predictions.
the relative performance of various greedy mapping algorithms is independent from sizable variances in expected run-time predictions.
the performance of various mapping algorithm is independent of sizable variations in the predicted run-time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of scheduling algorithms in distributed computing systems.
the performance of mapping algorithms in a distributed environment, in which run-times of tasks are not deterministic.
the performance of mapping algorithms in the face of run-time variances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of an intelligent greedy algorithm for mapping is beneficial, even if the expected completion times of the jobs are not deterministic.

, if the mapping problem is solved in a greedy manner using expected run-times, then the resulting schedules will perform as well as or better than those produced by the naive algorithms, even when the exact run-time for a job is not known in advance.
the relative performance of various algorithms for job assignment is independent of sizable variations in the run-time predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the use of run-time estimates to assign jobs to processors can be beneficial, even though the estimates are not deterministic, and even though the mapping algorithms are greedy.
the relative performance of the mapping algorithms is independent to a large degree of the variances in the run-times.
we show that the performance of various mapping algorithm is independent of sizable variance in run-time predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even though the expected run-time for completion is not deterministic, the use of intelligent greedy mapping algorithms is still beneficial.
, even when expected run times are not available, it is possible to develop mapping algorithms that are robust to run-time variances.

the relative performance of various algorithms for scheduling tasks on distributed systems is independent of sizable variations in run-time predictions, and that the use of greedy algorithms is beneficial, especially in systems with large numbers of machines.
